text: If you had to choose between your personal growth and your girlfriend, what would be your choice? This is a dilemma that one of my subscribers has. So he wrote me this. Hello, I have been in a relationship with my girlfriend for six months now, and we don't really have any major problems. We love each other and do a lot together. Originally, I wanted to find myself and work a lot on myself before getting a girlfriend, but it turned out that we ended up together, and that has slowed my progress a bit. I'm not very satisfied with the life I'm living right now. I want to make more money, work more on myself, and so on. She kind of holds me back in that sense, and I feel like I would rather go through this process on my own. I love her very much, and I don't even think about breaking up, which is why the situation is difficult for me. What should I do? Another concern is that my girlfriend somehow doesn't show me that she has eyes only for me, that I am her priority. I mean, she says that she loves me and all, but I still don't really feel that way. I hope you can help me. To that I answered, hey man, thanks for your question. The devil is really in the details here. First of all, what exactly does working on myself mean for you? Is it mainly career or money oriented? Because if that's the case, and you can find a healthy balance between working on yourself and being in a relationship, I don't see this as a major issue. Plenty of people manage to grow professionally and personally while being in a relationship. However, if you genuinely feel that the relationship slows you down and you can't balance the two, then you need to prioritize. You need to be honest with yourself about what matters more to you right now, and make a clear choice. Now, if by personal growth you actually mean growing as a seducer, getting better at dating, and exploring other options, then I think the honest thing to do is to break up with your girlfriend, be free, and go explore the world. That would be the most ecological way to handle it, instead of staying in a relationship while wanting something else. Now to the second point, where you say your girlfriend doesn't really have her eyes only for you. Again, nuances matter a lot here. If that simply means she has work, studies, career goals, hobbies, family, or friends, then that's normal. That is life, people should have things outside of the relationship. As long as she spends time with you, cares about you, and shows you through her actions that you are important to her, this is not a problem. But, if not having her eyes only for you means she's actively talking to other guys, going to parties without you, doing girls trips where boundaries get blurry, and similar things, then yes, this is a problem. In a healthy relationship, you care about the other person and try not to do things that you know might hurt them. If she ignores that, then I would seriously suggest rethinking the relationship. Maybe that's your sign to end it, focus on yourself, and move forward on your own. But once again, the devil is in the details. Then he actually came back with some details. Thank you for the answer. When I talk about working on myself, I mean many things. Finding myself, who I really am, and also achieving something career-wise and earning good money. I try to pursue this as best as I can while being in the relationship, but if it doesn't work and she slows down my process, then I will have to end it, because my future is much more important to me. When I talk about her not having eyes for me, I mean that I don't feel very important in her life. We recently had an argument because I didn't want to go to a party, and she did. And then she told me that if I don't go, she will go without me with her friends. That definitely made me feel bad, because if the situation were reversed, I would stay with her and not go to the party. That tells me something, that I'm not as important as I should be. Luckily, it's not the case that she talks to or flirts with other men, but maybe I just don't know about it yet, who knows. Thanks again for your help. And to this I wrote, yeah man, now with details it is more clear. Honestly, her going to party without you is already a bad sign, especially if she knew that it would make you feel bad. And yeah, how do you know she was not talking to other dudes if you were not there? I mean, it could be the case, but chances are she did. Coupled together, with you wanting to work on yourself, I would say end the relationship, concentrate on personal growth. You can use it is not you, it is me line to be more ecological, and then live your life solo. You can still go on dates and see other girl or girls have fun without serious relationship. And then, as cliche as it sounds, if you find a girl with whom you would actually want a relationship and who would fit your criteria, you would know it, and it would feel natural. To that he said, thank you Ben. So yeah guys, that's that. My name is Ilyas Abdullin. Hope it was informative and interesting. Thanks a lot, and bye.
